newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may fly Osaka route as China objection ebbs.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may fly Osaka route as China objection ebbs.

text.p: Taiwan said on Monday it may resume direct commercial flights to Japan's Osaka -- cut off after Tokyo jilted Taipei for rival Beijing in a 1972 diplomatic shakeup -- on an apparent easing of China's objections.
The transportation ministry said Japan had informed Taipei of its wish to resume the Taipei-Osaka route, a potentially lucrative link due to heavy Taiwan tourist flows to Japan.

"Japan's authorities have informed us of their wish to resume the route," a ministry official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters by telephone. "We are ready to talk whenever they give us a date."
No such talks were scheduled, the official added.
Local newspapers said China had given Tokyo a tacit go-ahead to resume the Taipei-Osaka route.
Beijing has considered Taiwan a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and insists that foreign states obtain its approval before exchanging flights with the island.
"We are dealing strictly with Japan. We will not comment on whatever happens between communist China and Japan," the Taiwan ministry official said.
The Taipei-Osaka route was terminated in 1972 after Tokyo switched diplomatic ties to Beijing from Taipei, accepting that the communist People's Republic of China was the sole Chinese sovereign.
Taiwan has maintained direct flight links and active trade ties with many countries despite Beijing's attempt to isolate it completely from the official international scene.
Taiwan already has direct air links with the Japanese cities of Tokyo, Fukuoka and Nagoya.
